antiPatterns.name: File-size refactor
antiPatterns.description: Treating line count as sufficient evidence that a module should be split.
observableIndicators: The proposal begins from file length rather than a responsibility boundary.
The split has no owner-approved contract or focused behavior evidence.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Stop or reframe around one validated responsibility and proof obligation.

antiPatterns.name: Universal domain-type collapse
antiPatterns.description: Forcing distinct workflow, persistence, transport, or provenance representations into one supposedly canonical type.
observableIndicators: Boundary-specific states disappear from types.
Mapping or validation responsibilities move into callers or unchecked casts.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Preserve explicit representations and mappings until the owner proves semantic identity.

antiPatterns.name: Adapter-parity flattening
antiPatterns.description: Making local and PostgreSQL adapters look identical by hiding transactions, locks, constraints, audit coupling, or compare-and-swap semantics.
observableIndicators: A least-common-denominator interface replaces PostgreSQL-only guarantees.
Parity is claimed from return shapes without failure and database-effect comparisons.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Share intended domain scenarios while keeping production database guarantees explicit.

antiPatterns.name: Audit extraction out of transaction
antiPatterns.description: Moving an audit write or actor/version attribution outside the transaction that protects the mutation.
observableIndicators: The domain write can commit before its audit event.
A generic post-commit helper owns audit persistence.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Reject the seam and retain transaction-local audit atomicity; extract only pure event construction when safe.

antiPatterns.name: Conflict/idempotency conflation
antiPatterns.description: Calling an optimistic conflict idempotent even though a retry does not return the original successful result.
observableIndicators: At-most-once conflict safety is described as replay idempotency.
Mutation identity and retry-result behavior are omitted.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Classify the command as replay-idempotent, conflict-safe, or deliberately non-retryable and test the exact result.

antiPatterns.name: Source-string safety theater
antiPatterns.description: Using source-text presence checks as proof of authorization, state, retry, audit, or failure behavior.
observableIndicators: A source.includes assertion substitutes for an executed allow or deny case.
The check still passes after a plausible behavioral defect is seeded.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Retain text checks only for static architecture shape and add executable behavior evidence for runtime properties.

antiPatterns.name: Assertion laundering into helpers
antiPatterns.description: Moving meaningful journey assertions into helpers until failures become hidden, optional, or coupled to implementation structure.
observableIndicators: Journey tests retain setup calls but lose user-visible assertions.
A helper can return successfully after the protected behavior breaks.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Preserve assertion identity, failure signal, and journey ownership; prove seeded defects still fail.

antiPatterns.name: Migration archaeology rewrite
antiPatterns.description: Editing an applied migration to make the current schema or refactor look cleaner.
observableIndicators: A checksum-pinned migration changes.
A refactor uses historical SQL edits instead of a forward migration and compatibility plan.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Reject the change; use an approved forward migration, rollback strategy, and compatibility rehearsal if schema change is truly required.

antiPatterns.name: Abstraction multiplication
antiPatterns.description: Adding factories, registries, wrappers, or compatibility layers that increase concepts without improving a proof obligation or boundary.
observableIndicators: More live paths or representations exist after a structural cleanup.
The new layer has no independent contract, caller need, or removal condition.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Prefer the smallest seam and reject layers that do not improve enforceability, comprehension, or recovery.

antiPatterns.name: Green by baseline absorption
antiPatterns.description: Regenerating or weakening a baseline so a regression is reclassified as accepted debt.
observableIndicators: The baseline changes without an independently reviewed improvement or policy decision.
A failing metric becomes green without the underlying behavior or structure improving.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Keep the failure visible or record an explicit owner-approved pre-existing disposition; never absorb it silently.

antiPatterns.name: Opportunistic cleanup scope creep
antiPatterns.description: Changing nearby files or responsibilities because they appear untidy rather than because they are in the approved audit.
observableIndicators: Changed files are absent from allowedChangePaths.
The stated purpose expands after implementation begins.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Stop, revert out-of-scope changes, and seek a separately reviewed slice if the work is genuinely needed.

antiPatterns.name: Agent self-approval
antiPatterns.description: Allowing the implementation agent to validate its own assurance model, dismiss adversarial findings, accept residual risk, or declare convergence.
observableIndicators: The same context authors and approves evidence.
Human disposition fields are absent or populated by an agent identity.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Require context-separated challenge and named human approval at every judgment boundary.

antiPatterns.name: Provenance erasure
antiPatterns.description: Treating extracted field values as the complete output and dropping source, candidate, confidence, model, review, or correction history.
observableIndicators: A mapper returns only canonical values.
Golden comparisons omit evidence locations or reviewer history.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Preserve the full provenance contract and compare it in characterization and replacement evidence.

antiPatterns.name: Identity by display name
antiPatterns.description: Turning matching names or other display attributes into an automatic canonical resident link.
observableIndicators: Name equality bypasses conflict blocking.
Ambiguous candidates are persisted without explicit human confirmation.
antiPatterns.requiredResponse: Reject automatic linking and preserve governed identifiers, conflict rules, optimistic review, and audit.
